newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed stronger on Tuesday at an eighth successive record high, but well back from peaks set during a mid-morning upward sprint before a softening dollar and profit taking began to weigh on the AEX index.

The morning's buying came largely from small investors inspired by a run of excellent Dutch corporate results, dealers said. They noted a growing mood of caution among institutional players after the Dutch market's recent heady rise.
Blue chip index heavyweights Royal Dutch and Unilever showed the clearest reversals on the day as investors moved to realise paper profits on the stocks' recent outperformance.

Unilever ended down 7.50 guilders, or around two percent, after rising over 13 percent during the last five trading days. An SBC Warburg "trading sell" rating today had also hit the stock, traders said.

Gainer of the day was warehouse equipment smallcap Nedcon Group, which unveiled solid profits for 1996 versus a loss the previous year and issued an optimistic forecast for 1997. The shares bounced nearly 20 percent to 65 guilders.
Trucking firm Frans Maas was on the losing end, dropping over five percent after disappointing results and the departure of the firm's chairman.

Retailing and services group Vendex had a see-saw session, jumping after it said 1996/97 profit was expected to rise strongly, but settling back later to end with a loss of around three percent on the day.
Midcap copier firm Oce booked a clear gain after its encouraging results on Monday. The shares finished 2.00 guilders higher, after standing more than eight ahead at one stage.
Further profit and sales growth is expected from the company in 1997 and the shares look attractive, one broker said. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
